newSources.said: 1.1. The Cayman Islands Film Commission (“CIFC”) is a government agency aligned with the Ministry of Tourism and Trade Development. … 2.1. Productions that commenced principal photography (filming) before 18th January 2024 are not eligible for the Rebate. … 2.10. Minimum CIQPE thresholds: • CI$250,000 across all eligible production categories. … 2.11. The Rebate is calculated as a minimum of 15% of CIQPE. 2.12. There is an uplift (additional rebate) worth 10% of CIQPE incurred on unscripted productions filmed in the Cayman Islands. 2.13. … 5% of CIQPE incurred on productions that are explicitly and visibly set in the Cayman Islands. 2.14. … 5% … that portray the Cayman Islands in a positive light, at the discretion of the Minister of Tourism. 2.15. … 5% … on productions that incur at least $1.5M in CIQPE and submit a plan for training Caymanians … 2.16. … 5% of CIQPE incurred on Cayman Brac or Little Cayman. 2.17. … 10% of CIQPE incurred on Cayman Islands resident Qualifying Local Vendors and Qualifying Local Labour … 2.18. The Rebates and uplifts (additional rebates) may be combined where eligible; however, the maximum Rebate for any individual CIQPE is capped at 35%. … 4.10. Fees paid to cast and other above-the-line personnel are limited to 25% of the total CIQPE.

newSources.title: Cayman Islands Film Commission: Incentive Programme
newSources.said: The Cayman Islands Government offers a cash rebate to eligible productions, calculated as a percentage of qualifying production expenditure incurred in the Cayman Islands. The rebate rate goes from 15 - 35%, depending on the type of production and whether it is eligible for certain uplifts. A rebate is normally payable within 90 days of a rebate claim being successfully processed. An interim certificate of approval is available to productions for financing purposes.
